name: Shibuya & Shinjuku
description: Sangenjaya to Shibuya, Shinjuku and Yotsuya from open data, lit by the real sun: Project PLATEAU's surveyed heights, the Shibuya scramble, the Suga Shrine stairs of Your Name, and the streets Persona 5 drew.

imagery.attribution: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, source attribution)

terrain.attribution: GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data DEM5A, 5 m airborne laser survey bare earth (GSI terms of use); 10 m DEM where 5A is absent

terrain_check.name: GSI elevation API (1 m laser DEM where flown, otherwise DEM5)

plateau.attribution: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)

water.note: No sea and no open river: the Shibuya River runs in a culvert under the station, and the ponds of Shinjuku Gyoen and Meiji Jingu are left to the aerial photo, since the viewer's water plane sits at sea level and the ground here is 20-45 m above it.

trees.note: Species are not mapped. Elms stand for the zelkovas (keyaki) of Omotesando and the shrine groves, plane trees for the street planes and ginkgos of Aoyama and Meiji Jingu Gaien. A guess, not a survey.

tour.title: Sangenjaya to Shinjuku, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height that Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's laser-scanned bare earth under GSI aerial photographs.

tour.title: The scramble
tour.text: Four streets meet at Shibuya's scramble, and when the lights change every crossing goes green at once, the diagonal too. The white bars are drawn from OpenStreetMap's crosswalks. Hachiko sits on his granite to the south.

tour.title: SHIBUYA SKY, 229 m
tour.text: On Scramble Square's roof (2019): about 2,500 m² of open deck at {landmark:shibuya_sky.deck_m} m, glass at the edge, GEO COMPASS in the middle and the escalator coming up out of the 46th floor.

tour.title: The stairs of Suga Shrine
tour.text: {landmark:suga.otokozaka.steps} stone steps, three and a half metres wide, red iron handrails both sides and down the middle: the 男坂 of Suga Shrine, the stairs of Your Name. The film turns ten this year.

tour.title: Sangenjaya's triangle
tour.text: Between Setagaya-dori and Route 246, the backstreets of Sangenjaya: a bathhouse, a snack bar, a meat shop open all night. A game drew its home town here and called it Yongen-Jaya.

tour.title: Kabukicho after dark
tour.text: Kabukicho Ichibangai's red arch has lit the way in since 1969. The district is named for a kabuki theatre planned after the war that was never built.

tour.title: Where the heights come from
tour.text: Blue: a surveyed height (PLATEAU or OpenStreetMap). Orange: a floor count. Green: an estimate from the neighbours. Towers finished since PLATEAU's survey, such as the Tokyu Kabukicho Tower, keep OpenStreetMap's height.

labels.キャロットタワー: Carrot Tower キャロットタワー

protection.title: No sun-access rule for public places
protection.summary: Tokyo protects no park's sunlight. The windows are a lunch-hour thought experiment for this project, as in the Marunouchi model.
protection.source_note: Windows are our own choice (noon to 13:00, all year), not law. The Building Standards Act's shadow rule (日影規制, art. 56-2) limits hours of shadow on neighbouring land in residential-type zones; it does not cover public places and does not apply in commercial districts such as Shibuya or Shinjuku.
protection.reading_note: Tokyo keeps standard time all year. Miyashita Park is a roof garden on a mall (2020): its sun here is read at the ground, so treat it with care.
protection.tip: Tip: try a tower on the block south of Yoyogi Park, or beside Shinjuku Gyoen's west gate.

sources.landmarks: Suga Shrine's 男坂 from the Tokyo stairs database (52 steps, 3.6 m, 16 m, 27°, red iron handrails); its hall, torii and furniture placed from OpenStreetMap and photographs; SHIBUYA SKY from SHIBUYA SKY and Wikipedia (229 m, 2,500 m², 18 searchlights, 360 m/min lifts); the Docomo tower's clock (15 m, 150 m up; Tokyo tourism, TV Tokyo) and mast (272 m; SkyscraperPage); Kabukicho's arch (1969; Sanshin Shoji). Signs, screens and shop fronts are indicative.
sources.fonts: Ema, plaques and signs drawn with Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Yomogi, Zen Kurenaido, Klee One, Yuji Syuku, Shippori Mincho, DotGothic16, RocknRoll One, Ma Shan Zheng, ZCOOL KuaiLe, Long Cang, LXGW WenKai TC, Nanum Pen Script, Caveat, Kalam

light_show.name: CROSSING LIGHT
light_show.note: SHIBUYA SKY's 18 searchlights on the roof light after sunset with the seasons (Wikipedia). Their times and movement here are illustrative.

game.title: Tokyo Pilgrimage 東京巡礼
game.blurb: Walk the real Shibuya and Shinjuku, rebuilt from open data and lit by the real sun: the scramble, SHIBUYA SKY 229 m up, Sangenjaya's backstreets, Kabukicho's arch and the stairs of Suga Shrine, ten years after a film and a game made them famous.

Shibuya's scramble at {time}. {sun_line}

{time}. I'm late. Again.

lines.title: Report back
lines.on_open: Every walk done. Report back to Aoi at Hachiko.

quests.title: Hachiko
talk: ようこそ渋谷へ! I'm Aoi. I guide pilgrims: people who come to stand where a story stood. This month it's ten years since a film and a game put these streets on the map.
This is the real Shibuya, rebuilt from open data: {buildings} buildings, {share:plateau}% of the footprint area at heights Project PLATEAU surveyed.
Hachiko has sat here since 1948. A game called this square Station Square. Walk out onto the scramble when the lights change.

steps.text: Meet Shun at the mouth of Center Gai

quests.title: Center Gai
talk: Center Gai. A game called it Central Street and gave it a burger bar that doesn't exist. The arch is real: go and read it.
See the glass passage over the crossing, on the station side? Okamoto Taro's thirty-metre mural, Myth of Tomorrow, hangs inside. A game made that passage a hideout.
For the view everyone came for, go up SHIBUYA SKY on top of Scramble Square. Yuna works the door.

steps.text: Read the arch over Center Gai
Find Yuna at SHIBUYA SKY's street door

quests.title: SHIBUYA SKY
talk: SKY GATE: the lifts run from 14F to 45F at 360 metres a minute. From the 46th floor an escalator takes you out into the open air.
The roof is about 2,500 square metres. The glass is lowest at SKY EDGE, over the scramble. No bags past 46F: the wind takes them.
Press E by the lift door. Or open the map: the roof is on your list of places to go.

steps.text: Ride the escalator out onto the roof
Stand at SKY EDGE, over the scramble

quests.title: SKY EDGE
talk: From up here the scramble is a clock face: everyone waits, then everyone goes.
GEO COMPASS, the raised deck in the middle, points at places you can't see: Mt Fuji, Skytree, Suga Shrine, even Paris and Sydney.
After dark, CROSSING LIGHT: eighteen searchlights. {sun_line}

quests.title: Sangenjaya
talk: Sangenjaya, three tea houses. In a game it's Yongen-Jaya, four: the same backstreets with one more tea house.
The game's café has the front of a snack bar here, New Marina. The bathhouse is Chiyo-no-yu, across the lane.
Take it slow. These are people's homes and small shops.

quests.title: Chiyo-no-yu
talk: Forty years a regular. The curtain says ゆ: hot water. Men on one side, women on the other.
Coin laundry beside it, vending machines out front. Everything a backstreet needs.
Come back after dark. The signs light up the triangle between Setagaya-dori and Route 246.

quests.title: The stairs
talk: 你好! I flew in from Shanghai for the tenth anniversary. These are the stairs from the poster: Suga Shrine's 男坂.
{landmark:suga.otokozaka.steps} steps, three and a half metres wide, red iron handrails on both sides and down the middle. Count them on the way up.

steps.text: Find Mr Sato by the torii

quests.title: Suga Shrine
talk: Suga Shrine has watched over Yotsuya's eighteen towns since 1634. The hall burned in the 1945 raids; the parishioners rebuilt it.
The great torii went up in 1990. The ema rack is full this year: a lot of them are for the film's tenth.
Read a few. Then, if you like, wait for dusk: the light the film was made of.

choices.text: Show me dusk on the stairs

steps.text: Read an ema on the rack
Stand at the foot of the stairs

quests.title: Shinjuku
talk: Shinjuku 2-chome: a few hundred bars, most of them the size of a living room. A game put a bar here where a journalist drank.
Kabukicho's arch has been red since 1969. Go and see it after dark, and say hello to Officer Ono at the koban.

quests.title: Kabukicho
talk: Kabukicho is named for a kabuki theatre planned here after the war. It was never built; the name stayed.
From the south side of the station you can see the Docomo tower's clock: {landmark:docomo.clock_d_m} metres across, {landmark:docomo.clock_z_m} metres up. You may know it from a film.

quests.title: Aoyama-itchome
talk: This is my stop. In a game a school stood up the road from here. There isn't one; I checked.
What's real: the ginkgo avenue of Meiji Jingu Gaien. 146 trees in four rows, nine metres apart, planted from 1908. They go yellow at the end of November.

steps.text: Walk the ginkgo avenue at Jingu Gaien

quests.title: Pilgrim
talk: お帰り! Stairs, a bathhouse, an arch, a roof 229 metres up. All of it real, all of it measured.
Ten years ago a film and a game drew these streets. Now you've walked them. Change the time, go up SHIBUYA SKY at night, or just wander.
